title: Opaque authorization failures on private clusters: SSO role mapping + KMS unwrap edge case
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: Multiple enterprise Private customers reported intermittent 403s and missing audit events after recent key rotations. Root cause (initial analysis): a narrow race combining a KMS envelope unwrap retry path with SAML NameID/role mapping normalization caused the control plane to treat some SSO assertions as unauthenticated for a short window. The unauthenticated path skips per-tenant audit event enrichment, producing gaps in audit logs and opaque RBAC failures on downstream services. Affected surfaces: - Private control plane SSO assertion processing - RBAC role lookup and enforcement (service-side) - Audit event streaming to customer audit sinks - KMS envelope unwrap and key rotation handling Reproduction steps discovered in staging: 1) Trigger a rotating key policy for tenant KMS (simulate rotation event). 2) Simultaneously re-auth a user via SAML SSO where NameID contains trailing whitespace or unusual format. 3) Observe KMS client return of transient 'decrypt: envelope invalid' followed by a retry; SSO handler receives assertion replay and the role mapper normalizes the NameID differently across retry, resulting in a failed role lookup and a 403 on token-introspect path. Impact: - A subset of SSO logins for Private customers become unauthenticated for ~5-20s during rotation windows. - Audit events emitted during the window lack tenant metadata and are dropped by downstream filters for some customers (compliance risk). - Several escalation threads opened by customers (Acme Health, Orion Payments, and one internal SOC partner). Immediate mitigation: - Control plane: enable a short-lived conservative fallback that queues SSO assertions until KMS unwrap completes (temporary feature flag: priv.sso.kms_block_on_unwrap = true). - Support playbook: instruct impacted customers to throttle management-plane rotations until patch lands and to optionally re-run manual assertion exchange; provided runbook link below. Long-term fix plan: 1) Patch SSO processing to canonicalize NameID consistently (trim/normalize unicode) before any caching or mapping steps. 2) Harden KMS client unwrap: add deterministic idempotent unwrap semantics, increase retry backoff, and surface unwrap-in-progress state to auth flow so role lookup waits on unwrap rather than proceeding as unauthenticated. 3) Ensure audit pipeline flushes and annotates events that happened during unwrap failures rather than dropping them. 4) Add unit and integration tests (KMS rotation + SAML edgecases) and a regression suite. Rollout plan: - Patch merged to main -> deploy to private-controlplane-staging (today 2026-03-14) for validation. - Canary: roll to 10% of Private clusters for 1 hour, monitor auth success rate and audit event integrity. - Full rollout to Reserved nodes and on-prem packages over 48 hours (target complete 2026-03-16). Monitoring & Success criteria: - Auth failure rate attributable to this path falls to 0% in canary (from ~0.6% observed). - Audit event completeness metric (per-tenant) returns to baseline. - No increase in 5xx control plane errors. Postmortem: capture timeline, root cause, and compensating controls; schedule a blameless RCA within 7 days of full rollout.

mitigation_steps: 1) Enable priv.sso.kms_block_on_unwrap feature flag for at-risk clusters. 2) Advise customers to postpone automated key rotations for 24-48h. 3) Turn on verbose audit buffering in control plane to retain events if downstream sinks reject them.
severity_summary: Intermittent auth failures and audit gaps during KMS rotations for Private customers causing compliance and access disruptions; urgent patch in progress.
